messages.text:
We propose replacing the adviser, copying and audit clauses with the following wording.

> The testing house may use the drawings and CAD geometry solely to prepare for, conduct and report on the agreed actuator vibration tests. Access is limited to test personnel listed by name in the test plan and approved in writing by the design owner. Each person must be bound by confidentiality and use restrictions at least as protective as this agreement. The same conditions apply to external test personnel. The testing house remains responsible for each approved person’s compliance. Additions and substitutions require written approval before access.
>
> The testing house may make the working copies reasonably necessary for the tests, encrypted in storage and in transit. It may extract the minimum geometry needed to design and make fixtures for these tests. The drawings, geometry, copies and derivative fixtures may not be used for another project or to develop a competing product.
>
> Within 30 days after the design owner accepts the final test report in writing, or after earlier termination of the tests, the testing house must securely erase the drawings, working copies and derivative fixture files, destroy the derivative physical fixtures, and provide a signed certificate confirming completion by the testing house and its approved external personnel. The testing house may retain the final report and measurement records if they do not disclose the CAD geometry.
>
> If the design owner identifies a specific discrepancy in the destruction certificate, the testing house may resolve it through certification by an independent verifier acceptable to both parties. The design owner has no on-demand right of site access.

Can your quality system retain the evidence needed to substantiate the test results without retaining fixture geometry? If a particular record or backup requires longer retention, please identify its contents, the required period and who would have access so we can agree on a narrow exception.

We can accept the deletion/certification structure in principle. We need two changes: a pre-approved backup/substitution path so one unavailable specialist does not stop the test, and a narrow calibration-record retention exception. We also need verification to be by appointment/remote review, with no access to the shared customer site.

Replace the access, retention and verification wording as follows:

> The testing house may use the drawings and CAD geometry solely to prepare for, conduct and report on the agreed actuator vibration tests. Access is limited to named test personnel and named external personnel identified in the approved test plan or an approved personnel list. Each person must be bound, directly or through their employer’s written undertaking, by confidentiality and use restrictions at least as protective as this agreement. The testing house remains responsible for each approved person’s compliance.
>
> The test plan may designate one or more backup personnel for each named role. Written approval of the test plan is approval of those designated backups for that role only. Any other addition or substitution requires written approval before access, and approval will not be unreasonably withheld or delayed.
>
> The testing house may make the working copies reasonably necessary for the tests, encrypted in storage and in transit. It may extract the minimum geometry needed to design and make fixtures for these tests. Each extract will be logged, limited to the interface or feature needed, and supplied to the specialist machining shop or other external personnel only as a standalone controlled extract, not with the full drawing set or CAD model.
>
> Within 30 days after the design owner accepts the final test report in writing, or after earlier termination of the tests, the testing house must securely erase the drawings, working copies and derivative fixture files, destroy the derivative physical fixtures, and provide a signed certificate confirming completion by the testing house and its approved external personnel.
>
> The testing house may retain the final report and measurement records if they do not contain or disclose the CAD geometry or fixture geometry. The testing house and its accredited calibration laboratory may retain calibration records required by the testing house quality system for two years from creation. Calibration records are limited to equipment identification, calibration dates, standards used, environmental conditions, as-found and as-left data, expanded uncertainties, statements of conformity and signatory. They will not contain CAD geometry, fixture geometry or drawing extracts. Access to those retained calibration records is limited to quality/calibration personnel and third-party auditors requiring access for accreditation.
>
> If the design owner identifies a specific discrepancy in the destruction certificate, resolution is by certification from an independent verifier acceptable to both parties. Verification is limited to confirming deletion/destruction against the certificate and related logs, by remote document review or a pre-arranged visit to the testing house’s premises during business hours. There is no on-demand site access, no unannounced access, and no access to any shared customer site or unrelated third-party information.

To make this operable, we propose three attachments:

1. Approved personnel and backup list.
2. Drawing/fixture extract log.
3. Destruction certificate form.

No backup containing drawings or geometry needs longer retention than the deletion period. The only longer retention is the calibration records described above, and they are retained without geometry.

We accept the proposed wording for named personnel and role-specific backups, controlled extracts, two-year retention of geometry-free calibration records, and independent verification. We agree to the three attachments and to remote review or a scheduled visit to the testing house’s premises, with no access to a shared customer site.

Please carry forward the express restriction on competitive use and make backup deletion explicit in the certificate. We propose these two sentences for the agreed text.

> Neither the testing house nor its approved personnel may use the drawings, CAD geometry, controlled extracts, derivative fixture files or physical fixtures for any other project or to develop a competing product.

> The signed destruction certificate must confirm that the testing house and its approved external personnel have securely erased all backup copies containing drawings or geometry within the same 30-day period.

We accept. Insert the competitive-use restriction as proposed, and make the certificate obligation explicit for backups and physical fixtures:

> Neither the testing house nor its approved personnel may use the drawings, CAD geometry, controlled extracts, derivative fixture files or physical fixtures for any other project or to develop a competing product.

> The signed destruction certificate must confirm that the testing house and its approved external personnel have securely erased all copies, including backup copies, of the drawings, CAD geometry, controlled extracts and derivative fixture files, and have destroyed the derivative physical fixtures, within the same 30-day period.

This keeps the retained calibration records outside the certificate because they contain no drawings or geometry. The three attachments remain as agreed.

We request a narrow addendum for the prototype batch. Only the geometry on page 4 of one drawing is export-restricted. We propose identifying that drawing by number and revision in the test plan and using a reference coupon for the affected test step.

> The design owner will withhold page 4 and supply a test copy that omits the restricted geometry. The testing house and its external personnel may use only that copy and owner-supplied files cleared for this test. If the testing house or any external recipient already holds the affected revision, the testing house will suspend use and onward transfer of that copy, notify the design owner, and coordinate secure deletion and written confirmation. Test work independent of the restricted geometry may proceed.
>
> The design owner will prepare a reference coupon free of restricted geometry within two days after both parties agree in writing on the verification test. Before using the coupon for the affected test step, the testing house will perform the agreed verification and record the result. If the coupon fails, the affected step will remain on hold pending written agreement on a correction.

We propose a low-level vibration sweep with the planned mounting and instrumentation, comparing the measured response against an owner-supplied, geometry-free acceptance envelope. Please confirm whether that comparison would qualify the coupon for the affected step and identify the response quantity, frequency range and tolerance you would need in the test plan. Please also confirm whether any recipient already holds the affected revision.

Please hold the cut stock and the earlier extract in quarantine at the machining shop pending our review. Have the shop confirm the extract identifier and revision and the corresponding stock identifier in writing, without sending the extract, dimensions or photographs. We will check our source records for any page 4 geometry and give written disposition instructions for both items. Until then, the shop must suspend machining, use and onward transfer. Any destruction must be recorded in the destruction certificate.

We propose the following qualification wording.

> The testing house will run a low-level vibration sweep on the identified coupon using the planned mounting, drive-point reference and one response accelerometer. The test plan will specify the frequency limits of the full planned test range, the evaluation frequencies and the design owner’s geometry-free reference values. At each evaluation frequency, the measured response-to-drive transfer function must be within ±1 dB of the reference magnitude and ±10 degrees of the reference phase, with coherence above 0.95.
>
> The two-day coupon preparation period begins when both parties approve the completed verification plan in writing. The test lead will submit the measured results against each criterion to the design owner. The affected step may proceed only after the design owner accepts a passing result in writing. A failed verification keeps that step on hold until both parties agree on a correction and the coupon passes verification. Verification and acceptance are additional to the preparation period.

The sweep is the proposed qualifying method. No shop repeatability check or transfer of feature tolerances is authorized. We accept the proposed coupon custody terms, including unique identification, design-owner ownership, secure storage at the testing house, no external transfer, and return or destruction at our direction after final report acceptance. Independent test work may proceed.

Please send the proposed frequency limits and evaluation frequencies with the quarantine identifiers. We will supply the geometry-free reference values for written approval of the completed plan.

We accept the qualification wording and coupon custody terms as proposed.

Quarantine identifiers:

- Extract: EX-ACT-FIX-001 Rev A
- Stock: STK-ACT-MAT-001

The machining shop has confirmed both identifiers in writing to us, without sending the extract, dimensions or photographs. Both items are quarantined there; machining, use and onward transfer are suspended.

On the current understanding that the full planned test range is 5 Hz to 2000 Hz, we propose frequency limits of 5 Hz to 2000 Hz and evaluation frequencies at 20, 50, 100, 200, 500, 1000 and 2000 Hz. If your records show a different planned range, please confirm and we will align the limits and evaluation frequencies.

Independent test work not involving the quarantined items will proceed.

We accept the proposed 5–2000 Hz sweep for the draft plan, subject to confirmation against the planned test range. Please include 5 Hz as an evaluation point so the pass criteria apply at both ends of the sweep. The resulting evaluation frequencies are 5, 20, 50, 100, 200, 500, 1000 and 2000 Hz.

We will confirm the range and supply geometry-free reference magnitudes and phases for each evaluation frequency in the completed plan. The two-day coupon preparation period begins upon both parties’ written approval of that plan. Use of the coupon in the affected step requires our subsequent written acceptance of a passing result.

Please keep EX-ACT-FIX-001 Rev A and STK-ACT-MAT-001 in quarantine pending our source-record review and written disposition. Independent test work may proceed.

We accept the evaluation frequencies: 5, 20, 50, 100, 200, 500, 1000 and 2000 Hz, with pass criteria applied at 5 Hz as a sweep end point. The test plan will state that after plan approval, no coupon preparation begins until both the geometry-free reference magnitudes/phases are supplied and the quarantined items are released by written disposition.

We will hold EX-ACT-FIX-001 Rev A and STK-ACT-MAT-001 in quarantine as follows:

> The identified items are physically and logically segregated. They will not be used, modified, copied, shipped or relied on for any test step until written disposition is received from the design owner. Independent test work using other approved items may proceed, but any step requiring the quarantined items or the coupon remains on hold.

Please provide written disposition before the planned coupon preparation period. If source-record review will take longer than the planned two-day preparation window, tell us now so we can resequence independent work and avoid a schedule conflict.

We accept the quarantine wording. Please revise the scheduling sentence so the source-record review can proceed in parallel with coupon preparation.

> The completed verification plan will include the confirmed sweep range and geometry-free reference magnitudes and phases at all eight agreed evaluation frequencies. Both parties’ written approval of that plan starts the design owner’s two-day coupon preparation period. Preparation and verification may proceed using approved materials independent of EX-ACT-FIX-001 Rev A and STK-ACT-MAT-001. The affected test step requires the design owner’s written acceptance of a passing verification result.

We cannot yet confirm a disposition date for the quarantined items. Please schedule on the basis that both remain unavailable. We will issue written disposition after reviewing the source records.

We accept that EX-ACT-FIX-001 Rev A and STK-ACT-MAT-001 remain unavailable for scheduling purposes; the schedule will assume no access to either.

The proposed sentence still ties the start of coupon preparation to confirmation of the reference values, which is the source-record review. To run the review in parallel, replace it with:

> The verification plan will state the sweep range and geometry-free reference magnitudes and phases at all eight agreed evaluation frequencies, marked provisional until the source-record review confirms them. Both parties’ written approval of that plan starts the design owner’s two-day coupon preparation period and permits the source-record review to proceed in parallel with coupon preparation and verification. Preparation and verification may proceed using approved materials independent of EX-ACT-FIX-001 Rev A and STK-ACT-MAT-001. The affected test step requires the design owner’s written acceptance of the confirmed sweep range and reference magnitudes and phases, and of a passing verification result.

We accept the proposed wording with one clarification for measurements taken while the plan values are provisional. Please add this sentence.

> If confirmation changes the sweep range or any reference value, the test lead will reassess the recorded measurements against the confirmed plan and repeat the sweep wherever the existing measurements are insufficient to demonstrate a pass.

Written approval of the provisional plan starts the two-day coupon preparation period. The quarantined items remain unavailable pending our written disposition.

We accept the proposed sentence and the related timing and quarantine terms:

> If confirmation changes the sweep range or any reference value, the test lead will reassess the recorded measurements against the confirmed plan and repeat the sweep wherever the existing measurements are insufficient to demonstrate a pass.

> Written approval of the provisional plan starts the two-day coupon preparation period. The quarantined items remain unavailable pending our written disposition.

These terms are agreed as test execution controls. They do not change the drawing access, use, controlled extract, deletion, or verification provisions already settled. The attachments remain as agreed.
